title: Settings page shows the four Require settings under Workflow, Line, Parts groups
preconditions:
1. You are signed in with access to Settings > App Settings.
2. Open the Work Order settings page.
steps:
1. Open Administration > App Settings (the Work Order settings page).
2. Read the setting labels and how the page is grouped.
expected:
1. The page shows four toggles: "Require ordering parts", "Require picking inventory parts", "Require receiving parts before completion", and "Require approval for new lines".
2. The page is grouped into "Workflow", "Line requirements" and "Parts", separated by dividers.
3. Every label reads in the "Require..." form, so turning one on always means more work.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8683 and story SV-9247 (Story 1, Work Order settings page) and the Simple Flow V2 specification version 21, read on 21 August 2026.

title: Require picking and Require receiving control their actions and defaults
preconditions:
1. You are signed in with Settings > App Settings.
2. You can toggle the picking and receiving settings and open an affected work order.
steps:
1. With "Require picking inventory parts" on, open a WO and check an inventory/found part; turn it off and check again.

2. Require receiving on: outstanding parts block the work order from being invoiced, and a Receive button sits on each part row. Off: outstanding parts do not block invoicing, and Receive moves into the part's ... menu.
3. Both default to on (their behaviour today).

title: A settings change applies to every open work order, not just new ones
preconditions:
1. You are signed in with Settings > App Settings.
2. Several open work orders exist in various statuses with outstanding parts and unapproved lines.
steps:
1. Turn "Require ordering parts" off and check outstanding parts across open work orders.
2. Turn "Require picking inventory parts" off and check outstanding inventory/found parts.
3. Turn "Require receiving parts before completion" off, then on, and check whether invoicing is blocked.
4. Turn "Require approval for new lines" off and check Needs-Approval lines.
expected:
1. The change applies to every open work order whatever its status, not only to work created afterwards.
2. Require ordering off: outstanding parts are recorded as ordered and the Order action disappears.
3. Require picking off: outstanding inventory and found parts are marked as picked and the Pick action disappears.
4. Require receiving off: outstanding parts stop blocking invoicing and stay outstanding, Receive moves to the ... menu. On: outstanding parts start blocking invoicing, nothing is auto-received, so a WO that was invoiceable may no longer be.
5. Require approval off: every line in Needs Approval becomes Approved (turning an estimate into approved work). On: lines already approved stay approved.
6. Statuses change in the underlying records, not only in the interface; invoicing checks the same state.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8683 and story SV-9248 (Story 2, Settings apply to every work order) and the Simple Flow V2 specification version 21, read on 21 August 2026.

title: An approved line completes whatever the state of its parts
preconditions:
1. You are signed in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and WO Lines: Create & Edit + Full View.
2. An approved line has parts that are unordered, unpicked and unreceived in various combinations, with each parts setting on.
steps:
1. On an approved line with an unordered part (ordering required), press Complete.
2. On an approved line with an unpicked inventory part (picking required), press Complete.
3. On an approved line with an ordered-but-unreceived part (receiving required), press Complete.
expected:
1. The line completes in every case; unordered, unpicked and unreceived parts do not prevent it, in any combination.
2. Ordering required, part never ordered: the line completes; the part stays waiting to be ordered.
3. Picking required, inventory part not picked: the line completes; invoicing still requires the pick, so the part is picked before the work order closes.
4. Receiving required, part ordered but not received: the line completes; the work order cannot be invoiced until that part is received or deferred with Received later.
5. Completing a line changes nothing about its parts — they keep whatever status the settings gave them.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8683 and story SV-9251 (Story 5, Parts no longer block completing a line) and the Simple Flow V2 specification version 21, read on 21 August 2026.

title: A line reaches Complete only through the defined paths

steps:
